correctness.rationale: For positive odd k, every composite maps to a prime and every odd prime maps to an even composite. A cyclic itinerary avoiding 2 therefore alternates and has even length. More generally any odd cycle needs a prime-to-prime step, necessarily 2→k+2; determinism gives uniqueness. Continuing the five-step itinerary forces 2k+2, then q=P⁺(k+1), then k+q. If q=2 the return was at step three; otherwise k+q≥4 is composite and maps to 2 exactly when it is a power of two. Conversely the stated conditions close the itinerary, and primeness, q>2, and q≤k+1<k+2 keep all five states distinct, including the two composites. The independent direct replay from 2 and largest-prime-factor arithmetic test agreed for all 100001 odd shifts through 200001, yielding exactly [5,21,51,59,1365,16271,87381].
residual_risks: The computation is only for the stated inclusive interval; classification for all positive odd k rests on the itinerary proof, not that scan.
